title: Our first look at the ASUS Googlebook shows Google's laptop plans taking shape
excerpt: Leaked images of the ASUS Googlebook CX9406 show an Aluminium OS laptop with Google's Glowbar and dedicated AI keyboard controls. First hardware evidence of what a Gemini-native laptop's physical UI looks like.
rationale: First actual hardware images of a Gemini-native laptop - the Glowbar and dedicated AI keys show how assistant-first computing reshapes physical UI.

title: BYD officially unveils AI robot Xiao Di - Tesla Optimus faces new rival as the U.S. blocks it
excerpt: BYD confirmed Xiao Di, a customer-facing humanoid robot debuting in its dealerships, just as the FCC moves to restrict Chinese humanoid imports. Humanoids are arriving as retail-floor interface hardware first.
rationale: A shipping humanoid deployed as a retail-floor interface rather than a lab demo - embodied AI becomes a customer-experience design surface.

title: Exclusive: Garmin Cirqa PM on launching a screen-free fitness tracker
excerpt: Garmin's product lead explains the design reasoning behind Cirqa, a screenless band whose coaching lives entirely in software rather than on the wrist. Screen-free wearables push the whole interface into the assistant layer.
rationale: A product lead walking through why the screen was removed - the clearest first-hand account of designing a wearable whose UI lives in the assistant.

title: DuckDuckGo anti-AI glasses offer zero cameras and notifications
excerpt: DuckDuckGo is pitching deliberately 'dumb' eyewear - no camera, no display, no notifications - as a counter-position to the AI glasses race. A rare anti-feature product design statement in a category where every vendor is adding sensors.
rationale: Subtraction as the product pitch - a rare anti-feature design position in a category racing to add sensors, and a usable argument for restraint.

title: I tried 3 self-hosted Claude alternatives on the same documents, and one crushed the others
excerpt: A head-to-head of three self-hosted document-chat stacks running locally finds the client tooling matters more than the model itself. A practical guide to keeping client files on your own hardware instead of a cloud assistant.
rationale: Directly actionable - a same-documents comparison showing studios how to run confidential client files through a local assistant instead of the cloud.
